chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you enter the Haram, take the Izkhir (fragrant grass) and chew it.' And he (peace be upon him) used to instruct Umm Farwa with that.

key_terms.أُمَّ فَرْوَة: Umm Farwa, a companion of the Imams to whom this instruction was directed
key_terms.الْإِذْخِر: Izkhir, a type of fragrant grass used for chewing and freshening breath
key_terms.الْحَرَم: The sacred precincts (Haram), referring to Mecca or the Prophet's mosque

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice regarding Izkhir when entering the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Sunnah of using Izkhir (a fragrant grass) to maintain oral freshness and remove odors before entering the sacred precincts, reflecting the emphasis on physical purity and etiquette in Shia jurisprudence. The specific mention of Umm Farwa, a prominent female companion, underscores the universality of this practice across genders within the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings. It serves as a practical guideline for enhancing the spiritual experience of worship through cleanliness and pleasant scent.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you enter the Harram, so take from the Izkhir (Fragrant grass) and chew it’. And heasws used to instruct Umm Farwaas with that’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ah ibn al-Hakam from Ah ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When you enter al-Haram (the sacred area), take from al-Idhkhir and chew it well.’ He (the Imam) would instruct ‘Umm Farwah to also do so.”
